transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you, too. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I'm just here because... well, things have been a little, I guess, unusual lately. I hope I'm explaining this right, but it's like my body feels a bit out of my control? 

A few weeks ago, I was just really energetic, you know? Like, pacing around my apartment all night, writing down all these ideas for a supper club I want to start. It was actually kind of great, I was getting so much done. But... well, lately it's sort of gone the other way. I'm just feeling really slowed down. My sister even pointed out that it takes me forever just to put my shoes on. It's probably nothing major, I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get back on track. Does that make sense?
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to hear or see?

Oh, um, no. No, nothing like that. I mean, sometimes at work—I'm a waiter—it gets really loud and I might think someone called my name over the noise, but that's just normal, right? But as far as, like, hearing voices or seeing things that aren't actually there... no, definitely not. I haven't had anything like that happen. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
During that energetic period, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual?

Um, not really? I mean, I was definitely staying up a bit later than usual because I was just so excited about writing down all those ideas, but I didn't feel like I didn't *need* sleep, if that makes sense. 

I still tried to get some rest before my shifts at the restaurant. I wasn't just running on empty or anything like that. I think my sleep was mostly okay, I was just choosing to stay up to work on my project. I hope that answers your question? I'm trying my best to remember exactly how it was, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
During that energetic period, did you feel unusually confident or like you had special abilities or importance?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I wouldn't say I thought I had superpowers or anything crazy like that. But, um... I did feel really, really good about my ideas. Like, I honestly believed I was about to build the best bilingual supper club in the city. 

I was just so sure of it, you know? I even thought that investors would be stupid not to back me. Looking back, I mean, I didn't even have a job or any money lined up, so it was probably a bit unrealistic of me to think that way. I hope it doesn't make me sound arrogant or anything? I was just really passionate about the project and I guess I got a little carried away. Is it normal to get that excited about a new idea?
Lately, have you been feeling that you’ve done something terribly wrong or deserve to be punished?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I mean, sure, I feel a little bad if I, you know, mess up an order at work or forget to call a friend back, but just normal stuff like that. I definitely don't feel like I've done anything *terribly* wrong, or... or like I deserve to be punished or anything. 

I always try really hard to do the right thing and be a good person. I hope that's okay? I just want to reassure you that I haven't been in any trouble or done anything bad. Did I answer that the way you needed me to?
Lately, have you been feeling depressed or down most of the day?

Um, well... I guess I've been feeling a little tired lately? But not, like, depressed all day or anything like that. I mean, everyone gets a little down sometimes, right? 

I just try to keep a positive attitude, especially at the restaurant. You have to smile for the customers, you know? I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping all day. I still get up and go to work and try to do a good job. I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I've been doing.
Lately, have you been feeling that your body or thoughts are being controlled by someone or something outside of you?

Oh, gosh, no. No, nothing like that. I mean, my thoughts are definitely my own. I wouldn't even know what that feels like, to be honest. 

I just... I just have normal thoughts, you know? Like what I need to do at work, or what I'm going to make for dinner. Just regular, everyday things. I hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm, like, totally out of touch with reality or something? Because I'm really not. I'm just a normal guy trying to do his best. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Lately, have other people noticed that you’re moving or speaking much more slowly than usual?

Um, well... I guess my sister did mention something the other day. She said it was taking me, like, forever just to get my shoes on to leave the house. But I don't think it's because I'm doing anything wrong, I just... my body kind of feels out of my control sometimes? 

Like, it's weird, because before this, I was actually moving a lot. I was pacing around my apartment all night, making all these notes for this supper-club idea I had. I was just so full of energy, you know? But now, yeah, I guess I have slowed down a bit. I hope it doesn't make me seem lazy or anything, because I really do try to keep up. I just feel a little stuck right now. Does that make sense? I hope that's an okay way to explain it.
When your body feels slowed down, do you feel sad or empty inside?

Um, no, not really sad. Or empty. I mean, I definitely don't want you to think I'm just, like, giving up or feeling hollow inside. I actually try really hard to keep my spirits up, you know? 

It's more just... my body feels heavy, I guess? But emotionally, I'm not miserable or anything like that. I always try to look on the bright side. I hope it's okay that I don't feel sad? I just don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is, and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Before these changes started, had you had any recent medical illness or head injury?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. No head injuries or... or major illnesses. I mean, I try to take really good care of myself, you know? I eat pretty healthy, and I'm on my feet a lot at the restaurant, so I get plenty of exercise. I haven't been sick or anything. 

I really hope I'm not doing something to cause all this, because I really do try to stay healthy. Is it... is it important that I haven't had a head injury? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so you can help me. I'm doing okay, right?
When your body feels out of control, do you ever get stuck in one position and have trouble moving at all?

Um, no, I don't think I get completely stuck. I mean, it's not like I'm frozen like a statue or anything, I promise. It's just... more of that heavy feeling I mentioned. 

I can still move, it just takes a little more effort sometimes. I definitely wouldn't say I'm entirely stuck. I try my best to keep moving, especially at work. I wouldn't want to leave my coworkers hanging, you know? So, no, I don't get stuck like that. I hope that's a good thing? I'm trying to be as helpful as I can with these answers.
When you feel slowed down, do you find yourself holding the same posture for a long time without meaning to?

Um, no... no, I don't think I do that. I mean, if I'm really tired after a long shift I might just sit on the couch for a bit, but I don't just... hold a weird pose without realizing it, I promise. 

I really try to stay aware of what I'm doing, especially around other people. I'd hate for my customers or my manager to think I was acting strange or, you know, just staring off into space in one position. So I always make an effort to look normal and keep busy. 

So, no, I definitely don't do that. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking so I can be a good patient for you.
Lately, have you been finding it hard to enjoy things you usually like?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I try really hard to stay positive, I really do. But lately... it's just been a little harder to get into the things I usually love. 

Like, normally I'm all about cooking, taking photos of the food, listening to music, playing pickup soccer... I even volunteer when I have time. Those things usually keep me really steady. But right now, they just feel kind of... flat? Like, I know I used to care about them a lot, but I just can't seem to make myself feel it right now. 

I'm still trying, though! I promise I haven't just given up. I'm hoping it's just a phase and I'll bounce back soon. Does that make sense? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy or ungrateful. I really want to get back to enjoying things again.
During this slowed-down period, have you been feeling hopeless?

Hopeless? Um... no, no, I wouldn't say hopeless. That sounds a bit too... dark, I guess? 

I really try my best to keep my chin up, even when things are feeling kind of heavy or flat. I mean, I know things will get better eventually, so I promise I haven't given up at all. I have to keep a good attitude for my tables at the restaurant anyway, so I really try not to let myself go to that kind of place. 

So... no, definitely not hopeless. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to reassure you that I'm really trying to work through this and do whatever I need to do to get better.
During this slowed-down period, have you still been feeling unusually cheerful or high?

Um, cheerful? No, no, definitely not right now. 

I mean, I know I'm usually a pretty upbeat guy—I have to be for work, you know? You can't be dragging your feet when you're waiting tables. But lately, with everything feeling so slow and flat, I haven't had any of those... really high highs. 

I really hope I'm not sounding too negative today. I'm usually much more positive, I swear. I just... I haven't felt that kind of super cheerful energy in a while. I'm just kind of... here, trying to get through the days. Is that the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
During that very energetic period, did your behavior cause serious problems at work or in your relationships?

Um... well, "serious problems" sounds a little intense. I mean, I really try to be responsible, I do. But... I guess things did get a little bit messy during that time. 

I just had so much going on, you know? So many ideas and things I wanted to do. But... I guess I kind of dropped the ball on a few things. Like, my work schedule got a little confused, and... well, my rent arrangement got a bit complicated. I didn't mean for it to happen, I swear. I just lost track of time and details because I was focused on all these other big things. 

And, um... my family got a little worried. I guess I wasn't keeping up with my commitments to them either. Actually, my sister... she's the one who brought me to the crisis clinic. She said I wasn't organizing my basic responsibilities very well on my own. I felt really bad about it, honestly. I never want to be a burden on anyone. 

Does that... does that answer your question? I really hope it doesn't make me sound like a completely irresponsible person. I usually have things much more together than that.
About how many days in a row did that very energetic period last?

Um... how many days? I'm trying to think back... I really want to give you an exact number, but it's a little fuzzy. 

I know it was definitely going on for a while, but I wasn't really marking it on a calendar or anything, you know? I was just so busy with everything I was trying to accomplish. It felt like a good stretch of time where I was just... really productive and on the go. 

I'm sorry I can't be more specific. Is it okay if I don't remember the exact number of days? I hope that's not unhelpful. I just don't want to guess and give you the wrong information.
Did that very energetic period last a full week or longer?

Um... a full week? I mean, I guess it could have been. It's hard to say for sure, but yeah, it probably stretched out for at least a week, maybe a little more. 

I just remember feeling like I had this constant flow of energy for a while there. I wasn't really sleeping much, but I felt fine, you know? Like I could just keep going and going. I was getting so much done, or at least it felt like I was. 

I really hope it's okay that I can't pinpoint the exact start and end dates. I know you're trying to figure this all out, and I want to be as helpful as possible. Does a week or so sound like the right kind of timeline for what you're asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
